# Commit Message Instructions

Generate commit messages in English using the Conventional Commits specification.

## Structure

The commit message must have this structure:

<type>(<scope>): <description>

- <change>
- <change>
- <change>

## Commit title

The first line must follow the Conventional Commits format:

<type>(<scope>): <description>

Use one of these commit types when applicable:

- feat: A new feature or user-facing capability
- fix: A bug fix
- refactor: Code restructuring without changing behavior
- perf: A performance improvement
- docs: Documentation-only changes
- test: Adding or modifying tests
- chore: Maintenance changes that do not affect application behavior
- build: Changes to the build system or dependencies
- ci: Changes to CI/CD configuration
- style: Formatting or stylistic changes that do not affect behavior

Use a scope when the affected area can be identified clearly.

The description must:

- Be written in English.
- Use the imperative mood.
- Be concise and specific.
- Describe the main purpose of the commit.
- Not end with a period.
- Not include unnecessary details.
- Not include emojis.
- Not include a ticket or issue number unless it is explicitly present in the branch name or changes.

Keep the commit title reasonably short, preferably under 72 characters.

## Change breakdown

After the commit title, provide a bullet-point breakdown of the changes.

Each bullet must:

- Describe a meaningful change introduced by the commit.
- Be concise and specific.
- Use the imperative mood.
- Be written in English.
- Focus on what was changed rather than listing individual files.
- Avoid repeating the commit title.
- Avoid implementation details that are irrelevant to understanding the change.

Do not include a bullet for every modified file. Group related changes into a single bullet.

## Accuracy

Base the commit message only on the actual changes in the working tree and staged changes.

Do not invent functionality, behavior, fixes, or motivations that are not supported by the changes.

If multiple unrelated changes are present, reflect the primary purpose of the changes and summarize the secondary changes in the bullet list.

Do not mention that the message was generated by AI.
